item.title: February Exhibit "Roses Are Red" Opens at Charleston Crafts Gallery
item.description: Charleston Crafts Gallery, an artist-owned cooperative in the heart of downtown Charleston, is pleased to present its February exhibition, Roses Are Red, which opens with a public reception on Friday, February 6, from 5pm to 8pm.

item.title: Local Legislators Endorse Nick Uricchio’s Campaign for House District 115
item.description: Democratic candidate for South Carolina House District 115 Nick Uricchio today announced he has received enthusiastic endorsements from four local legislators, including the district’s current representative, Spencer Wetmore.

item.title: Katsubō Announces Super Bowl Wings Deal
item.description: Katsubō has announced game-day wing deals for the upcoming Super Bowl. Orders will be available for pickup Saturday, Feb. 7, 2026, the day before the big game.

item.title: The Darling Oyster Bar Celebrates Ten Years in Charleston
item.description: The Darling Oyster Bar will celebrate a major milestone next month, marking 10 years on King Street on Feb. 26, 2026.

item.title: Kiawah Island Golf Resort Hosting Career Fairs
item.description: Kiawah Island Golf Resort will host a series of on-site career fairs at Mingo Point, located at 876 Kiawah Island Parkway on Johns Island.

item.title: Comedian Lauren Hope Krass Returns To Theatre 99 With Viral Internet Sensation Jessie Jolles
item.description: Theatre 99 is pleased to welcome Lauren Hope Krass back to her home stage. For those familiar with local comedy lore, you may remember Lauren from placing twice in the Charleston Comedy Festival’s Stand Up Competition in the early 2010’s

item.title: Celebrity Culture and Public Perception of Cosmetic Surgery
item.description: Celebrities used to treat cosmetic surgery like a state secret. They would disappear for three weeks and return with tighter skin and a "rested" look that they credited to water and kale.

item.title: 5 Steps to Opening a High-Yield Savings Account
item.description: Your money works hard for you, or at least it should. Keeping cash in a standard checking account usually means it sits there, stagnant, losing value against inflation over time. Moving those funds into a specialized account designed to accumulate interest allows your balance to grow simply through the passage of time.

item.title: 23 Educators from 8 States Selected for Advanced-Level Education Program Focused on Teaching the Holocaust to the AI Generation
item.description: The Jewish Foundation for the Righteous (JFR) selected 23 middle and high school educators and Holocaust center staff from eight states to participate in its 2026 Advanced Seminar, an intensive two-day academic program
